existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` is removed from the R6 resource set, so R4 instances are not directly valid R6. The top migration concerns are resource identity replacement, required R6 lifecycle status, ingredient/device representation changes, and successor-only route/product constraints. The main uncertainty is the exact official migration intent because no computable cross-version map was available locally.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should not attempt a simple `resourceType` rename. A safe migration needs to construct an `AdministrableProductDefinition`, assign a publication `status`, map dose form and route content, decide whether ingredients remain simple codes or become `Ingredient` resources, move manufactured item context to `ManufacturedItemDefinition`/`producedFrom`, and move co-packaged devices to packaging/product-level structures where appropriate. R6-to-R4 conversion is also lossy because R6 has optional dose form and new product/manufacturing links that R4 `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` cannot carry directly.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the R4 resource is absent in R6 and treated as an old type. Confidence is medium for detailed element-by-element migration recommendations because they infer successor mapping from local R6 StructureDefinitions rather than an official R4-to-R6 ConceptMap or narrative migration guide. Terminology impact is limited by absent expansions, but most R6 bindings on retained coded fields are example-strength and therefore not direct validation breaks.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
MedicinalProductPharmaceutical has a resource-identity break: MedicinalProductPharmaceutical has no R6 StructureDefinition and is treated as an old resource type. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 94/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.

topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 instances with `resourceType: MedicinalProductPharmaceutical`, REST routes, references, generated classes, and FHIRPath roots have no same-name R6 base resource.

topFindings.title: Likely successor requires a new modifier lifecycle status
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid on the successor plus runtime/API/codegen: a migrated APD without `status` fails R6 validation, and modifier-aware consumers must account for non-active states; R6-to-R4 loses the status unless carried outside native R4 MPP.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Ingredient changed from references to a split code-or-Ingredient model
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and R6-to-R4 loss: an R4 `ingredient.reference` cannot populate APD `ingredient` directly, while an R6 coded ingredient or incoming `Ingredient` graph may not round-trip to an R4 reference without creating synthetic target resources.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid for R4 arrays with more than one device, plus semantic/conformance risk when a single R4 accompanying device is actually co-packaged rather than integral.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
